title: codemother's launcher words become scripts in its bin
intention: Each word codemother's self-named launcher consumes today — cross, watch, question, seed, show — is its own executable script in cairn/devices/codemother/0/bin carrying the arm's body unchanged, with a first comment line naming what it does, and the launcher keeps only its no-argument behaviour.
why: Measured 2026-11-05: cairn/devices/codemother/0/bin/codemother:9-90 dispatches cross, watch, question, seed and show in a case statement; under parent 41a70e789682 a word with no script goes onto the bus, so these would be stranded. Akien 2026-11-05 (Q#27, outline 8.4): 'if there's a script for it, run it, else get on the bus' and 'cairn help lists [all] then [operator] then [cairn] then the rest in alpha order'.
traces_to: Telos: the operator's one interface (outline 8.4). Law 1 (a shortcut is a settled route), Law 4 (script-else-bus is the dispatch, not a convention), RULE 1 (the bus is a device's public interface).
how: Move each case arm into bin/<word> verbatim (REPO_ROOT computed the same way), add the '# cairn codemother <word> — <what>' line, reduce the launcher to its default arm; red-first proof compares each word's output before and after on a read-only invocation.
falsifier: (1) each of cross, watch, question, seed, show is an executable in cairn/devices/codemother/0/bin whose first comment line names it; (2) `cairn codemother show <a standing artifact id>` prints byte-identical to HEAD; (3) the launcher contains no case arm for any of the five words.

decisions.text: Red-first proof cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_launcher_words_are_scripts.py, check()/FAILURES/main() shape, one tooth per falsifier clause, PROVES = {'ed3d02b24675': {'1': 'clause_1', '2': 'clause_2', '3': 'clause_3'}} (tooth names written at build). Scratch roots only — no live bus, no live store.
